identity.title: Covered Forest: Fine-grained generalization analysis of graph neural networks
identity.authors: Antonis Vasileiou; Ben Finkelshtein; Floris Geerts; Ron Levie; Christopher Morris
identity.page_convention: PDF page numbers, one-based, matching printed pages unless stated.

summary: Four demonstrated core defects in statistical normalization, sample-selected partition concentration, classwide continuity and zero-padding Lipschitz proof.
limitations: Full appendix and external cited-theorem audits incomplete

problems.title: Table1 statistical term divides by m instead of sqrt(sample size)
problems.claim: Estimated generalization bounds in Table1 instantiate Propositions15/16 and show tightness
problems.assumptions: Published/script coefficients; delta.05; integer k1..100 held fixed for comparison
problems.check: Parent direct source read and independent scalar reconstruction, corroborating auxiliary calculation
problems.result: All8 rounded entries reconstructed from wrong denominator; corrected diagnostics far larger
problems.counterevidence: Constants openly estimates; actual model gaps not refuted; historical checkout not proved; correction alone not certificate
problems.impact: Principal quantitative tightness evidence is arithmetically invalid
problems.core_dependency: Main empirical claim that theoretical bounds closely track real gaps
problems.correction: Use sqrt(S), validate constants/cover scope/radius; no repaired certified bounds claimed

focused_check.note: Verified the published statistical term and all eight table entries against independently reconstructed scalar arithmetic. The release divides outside the square root by m instead of sqrt(sample size), materially invalidating the claimed tightness evidence and supporting Major. Corrected same-k and reoptimized values are diagnostics, not certified risk bounds; estimated constants and dataset-dependent cover counts remain limitations.

problems.title: Sample-dependent cells invalidate multinomial concentration
problems.claim: Main Theorem4 permits a per-sample partition; Theorems35/37 are affected under that same interpretation, while Definition34 admits a narrower fixed-partition reading.
problems.assumptions: 1000 finite path classes, iid uniform100 samples, bounded loss1, K2, epsilon.001, delta.05
problems.check: Analytic memorization counterexample and exact scalar bound
problems.result: Main Theorem4: every-sample gap >=.9 versus .29704143746. Same counterexample applies to cell-specific statements only under the per-sample-partition interpretation.
problems.counterevidence: Definition34 wording permits a fixed sample-independent partition, which excludes this witness and can support ordinary concentration; later genuinely fixed-cover cases may survive.
problems.correction: Fixed partition or valid uniform partition complexity penalty

focused_check.note: Verified the sample-selected two-cell partition witness with fixed K=2, zero empirical loss and population loss at least 0.9 versus a bound about 0.29704. Fixed-partition multinomial concentration does not justify the main sample-dependent quantifier. Major applies to that core theorem/proof. Appendix Definition 34's narrower fixed-partition reading excludes the witness and is explicitly retained.

problems.title: No common modulus across unrestricted internal gains
problems.claim: Theorem8/43 common gamma for all n and stated architectures
problems.assumptions: L1, initial1, phi=n^2x, bounded1-Lipschitz tanh readout, edge versus empty graph
problems.check: Exact tree-distance2 and analytic outputgap tanh2; independent parent numbers
problems.counterevidence: Fixed networks and bounded internal gains may allow moduli; external cited paper not audited
problems.core_dependency: Common modulus for subsequent unlabeled-graph bounds
problems.correction: Bound internal gains/features or expose full-architecture dependence

focused_check.note: Verified the allowed n^2-gain family has normalized graph distance tending to zero while tanh(2) output separation stays above one half, also with an extra tanh readout. Absence of a common internal Lipschitz bound invalidates the core class-wide equicontinuity claim, supporting Major. Fixed-network continuity and the unread external theorem are not refuted.

problems.title: Forest-distance padding omits zero-preserving updates
problems.claim: Lemma14/57 Lipschitz bound for all allowed sum-aggregation updates
problems.assumptions: Fixed L2 identity-weight network phi1=x+1 phi2=x, tanh; positive real features; separate one-hot example
problems.check: Analytic exact forest costs and network recurrence, parent source-image and arithmetic checks
problems.result: FD=4a ->0 but outputgap ->.202433; one-hot n100 claimed.08 vs actual.96803
problems.counterevidence: Mean aggregation positive homogeneity and bias-free zero-preserving updates avoid this obstruction
problems.impact: False metric Lipschitz guarantee underpinning central sum-aggregation bounds
problems.correction: Zero-preserving updates or appropriate offset terms; complete repair unverified

focused_check.note: Verified the fixed-network positive-feature and one-hot affine-update witnesses satisfy the allowed unit-Lipschitz sum setting yet violate the stated forest-distance bound. The padding proof needs zero preservation and feeds core Propositions 15-16, supporting Major. Mean-aggregation restrictions cannot be imported into the sum setting; zero preservation is only a candidate condition, not an arbitrary-depth repaired proof.

repair_verification: Local restrictions and denominator corrections described; no global repaired theorem or statistical certificate certified.
